chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Walladin, and someone else from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever shall incline therein to wrong unjustly'
He said: 'The one who worships other than Allah Mighty and Majestic in it, or befriends other than the Guardians of Allah in it, so he is one who inclines to injustice unjustly'
And it is upon Allah Blessed and High to make him taste of a painful chastisement

key_terms.إِلْحَادٍ: Inclination or deviation, specifically towards injustice or misguidance

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'inclining to injustice' in the context of worshipping other than Allah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the phrase 'inclining to injustice' in Surah Al-Hajj by specifying it as introducing shirk or allegiance to non-divine authorities within the sacred precincts. This interpretation highlights the Kaaba not merely as a site of monotheistic worship but as a focal point where deviation from divine guardianship constitutes a grave injustice, warranting painful chastisement. The explanation underscores the Shia emphasis on *Wilayah* as integral to the purity of worship in the holiest sanctuary.
